statement: Define dur(i) = logs[i][1] - (if i = 0 then 0 else logs[i-1][1]) for 0 <= i < m, and let M = max { dur(i) | 0 <= i < m }. The function returns a result r and: (a) 0 <= r < n; (b) there exists i with 0 <= i < m such that logs[i][0] = r and dur(i) = M; (c) for every i with 0 <= i < m and dur(i) = M, we have r <= logs[i][0].
preconditions: Let m = len(logs). We assume 2 <= n <= 500, 1 <= m <= 500, for every i with 0 <= i < m the vector logs[i] has length 2, 0 <= logs[i][0] <= n-1, and 1 <= logs[i][1] <= 500, for every i with 1 <= i < m we have logs[i-1][1] < logs[i][1], and for every i with 0 <= i < m-1 we have logs[i][0] != logs[i+1][0].
